title: Tensor base change for a bounded below complex of Tor amplitude ≥ n
statement: Let $K$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a finite ring whose exponent is invertible in $K$. Consider schemes and morphisms $X\xleftarrow{p}X'\xleftarrow{h}Y$, $X\xrightarrow{a}\operatorname{Spec}K\xleftarrow{b}S'\xleftarrow{g}T$, $f'\colon X'\to S'$, $e\colon Y\to T$ with both squares cartesian ($X'=X\times_KS'$, $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$) and $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $E\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $F\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ be bounded below [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and suppose $E$ has Tor amplitude in $[n,\infty)$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude]: $H^q(E\otimes^LM)=0$ for every sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules $M$ and every $q<n$. Then the base change map $Lp^*E\otimes^LLf'^*Rg_*F\to Rh_*(Lh^*Lp^*E\otimes^LLe^*F)$ [def-kun-derived-tensor] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For any coefficient ring $R$ write $A_R(E,F)=p^{-1}E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(f')^{-1}Rg_*F$ and $B_R(E,F)=Rh_*(h^{-1}p^{-1}E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}e^{-1}F)$. Write $\alpha_R:A_R\to B_R$ for the adjoint of $1\otimes e^{-1}\varepsilon_g$, using the cartesian-square identity and the monoidal pullback identification [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. Exactness of inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identify the displayed inverse images with the derived pullbacks in the statement. Both functors are triangulated in each variable by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated], and [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The counit formula is natural in both variables and respects the shifts and the short-exact-complex triangles; the same monoidal identifications and $1\otimes\varepsilon_g$ give the map on each vertex. We use the resulting morphisms of triangles throughout, with [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] and [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. Right direct image preserves every lower cohomological bound: forget coefficients using [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison] and apply [lem-kun-tensor-t-est]. All sites are taken small in the fixed module universe [def-weil-size-convention].

Apply [lem-kun-0f1m] over $\Lambda$ to obtain a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $E$, zero below $n$, whose pullbacks have the same properties. Choose $b$ with $F\in D^{\ge b}$. For $N\ge n$ put $P_N=\sigma_{\le N}P$ and $T_N=\sigma_{\ge N+1}P$ [def-kun-truncations]. The sequence $0\to T_N\to P\to P_N\to0$ is degreewise split exact, also after any pullback. The bounded flat complex $P_N$ is K-flat [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1). The tails and their pullbacks are K-flat as well: tensor this split sequence with an arbitrary acyclic complex. It stays degreewise split exact after direct-sum totalization; the middle and final terms are acyclic, hence the first is acyclic by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. The original split sequence gives a triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle].

source.place: Tag 0F1J, first reduction paragraph; Tag 0F1M, sites-cohomology lemma-bounded-below-tor-amplitude

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], represent $F$ and $Rg_*F$ by complexes zero below $b$; the latter bound was proved in Step 1. The K-flat tails compute the tensors in $A_\Lambda(T_N,F)$ and inside $B_\Lambda(T_N,F)$ by [def-kun-derived-tensor]. These tensor complexes are zero below $N+1+b$, and Step 1 gives the same bound after $Rh_*$. For $q<N+b$ both degree $q$ and degree $q+1$ of either tail image vanish. The long exact sequences of Step 1 therefore identify $H^q(\alpha_\Lambda(E,F))$ with $H^q(\alpha_\Lambda(P_N,F))$. Choose $N>q-b$ for each fixed $q$. Repeated stupid-truncation short exact sequences decompose the bounded complex $P_N$ into shifts of its single flat terms; their triangles [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] and Step 1 reduce its comparison to those terms. It suffices to treat a flat sheaf $\mathcal E$ on $X$ in degree zero. This argument uses finite truncations and explicit bounds, not convergence of an infinite filtration.

The sheaves $p^{-1}\mathcal E$ and $h^{-1}p^{-1}\mathcal E$ are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback], with the constant-ring identifications of Step 1. Tensoring with either is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and commutes with cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]; the one-term complexes are K-flat [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1). Choose a representative $I$ of $F$ zero below $b$ [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Put $J_M=\tau_{\le M}I$ and $C_M=I/J_M$ [def-kun-truncations], with $M\ge b$. The quotient is zero below $M$, including the possible term $I^M/\ker d^M$ in degree $M$. The sequence $0\to J_M\to I\to C_M\to0$ gives a triangle [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Exact tensor and the lower direct-image bound put both comparison functors on $C_M$ in $D^{\ge M}$. For $q<M-1$ the long exact sequences identify the comparison on $I$ with that on $J_M$. The bounded complex $J_M$ is a finite extension of shifts of its sheaf terms through stupid truncations. Step 1 reduces its comparison to those sheaves. It suffices to prove the assertion when $\mathcal E$ is flat and $\mathcal F$ is any $\Lambda$-sheaf, both in degree zero.

A finite commutative ring is Artinian, since a strict descending chain of ideals strictly decreases finite cardinalities. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ideal-length-one-filtration] to its unit ideal to obtain $0=I_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq I_r=\Lambda$ with simple quotients $L_i=I_i/I_{i-1}$. For each $i$ choose $0\ne x_i\in L_i$. Simplicity makes $\Lambda x_i=L_i$; the kernel $\mathfrak m_i$ of $a\mapsto ax_i$ gives $L_i\cong\Lambda/\mathfrak m_i$. This quotient is a field: a nonzero residue $c$ acts with nonzero image on the simple module, hence surjectively, so $cdx_i=x_i$ for some $d$, giving $cd=1$ modulo $\mathfrak m_i$. Thus $k_i=\Lambda/\mathfrak m_i$ is a finite field and $\mathfrak m_i I_i\subseteq I_{i-1}$. Its characteristic $\ell_i$ is prime and divides the additive exponent of $\Lambda$ (the exponent kills $1$ in every quotient), hence $\ell_i$ is invertible in $K$. When $\Lambda$ is the zero ring, $r=0$ and every sheaf in the assertion is zero.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, reduction to prime torsion, generalized by finite-ring devissage; algebra.tex Tags 00JB (lemma-artinian-finite-length) and 00J2 (lemma-characterize-length-1), elementary cyclic-simple argument written out

proof.text: Let $I_i\mathcal F$ be the subsheaf generated by products $a s$ with $a\in I_i$ and local sections $s$ of $\mathcal F$. This gives a finite filtration from $0$ to $\mathcal F$. Its quotient $Q_i=I_i\mathcal F/I_{i-1}\mathcal F$ is killed by $\mathfrak m_i$, because $c(as)=(ca)s$ with $ca\in I_{i-1}$ for $c\in\mathfrak m_i$. Hence $Q_i$ is a $k_i$-module sheaf. The short exact sequences of this filtration give triangles [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], so Step 1 reduces the comparison for $\mathcal F$ to those for $Q_i$. Apply [lem-kun-flat-coefficient-tensor-exchange-comparison] to $\Lambda\to k_i$, $M=p^{-1}\mathcal E$, and $N=Q_i[0]$. It identifies this precise comparison with scalar restriction of the $k_i$-comparison whose first factor is $\mathcal E_i=\mathcal E\otimes_\Lambda k_i$. Pullback commutes with this scalar-extension tensor by the constant-ring identifications and monoidality of Step 1. Flatness of $\mathcal E_i$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback] applied to the identity topos with coefficient map $\Lambda_X\to(k_i)_X$. Restriction of scalars reflects isomorphisms by the coefficient comparison node. We have reduced to two sheaves over an arbitrary finite field $k$ of characteristic $\ell$ invertible in $K$.

For the extension $\mathbf F_\ell\hookrightarrow k$, [lem-pur-finite-field-derived-tensor-summand] supplies $z=\sum_j a_j\otimes b_j\in k\otimes_{\mathbf F_\ell}k$ with $\sum_j a_jb_j=1$ and $(c\otimes1)z=(1\otimes c)z$. If $V$ is a $k$-sheaf, put $\widetilde V=(U V)\otimes_{\mathbf F_\ell}k$, with $k$ acting on the last factor. The local formulas $s(v)=\sum_j a_jv\otimes b_j$ and $t(v\otimes c)=cv$ define natural $k$-linear sheaf maps $V\xrightarrow{s}\widetilde V\xrightarrow{t}V$. The displayed relation for $z$ gives $s(cv)=c s(v)$ and its multiplication identity gives $ts=1$. Additivity and the balancing relations give the maps before sheafification, and the formulas commute with every restriction, so they extend to sheaf tensors. This explicitly constructs the required retract using only the cited element.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, vector-space case, extended to finite fields using algebra.tex Tag 0C2X (lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal) and the existing finite-field tensor summand

proof.text: Let $V$ and $W$ be the two $k$-sheaves remaining in Step 6. Every $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf is flat by [lem-exc-constant-field-module-flat], applied on a small skeleton of the small etale site in the module universe. Thus $(UV)[0]$ has Tor amplitude $[0,\infty)$: its one-term complex is K-flat [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1), and its tensor with a degree-zero sheaf is concentrated in degree zero [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Both $UV$ and $UW$ are bounded below. Apply [lem-kun-0f1j] with integer coefficient modulus $\ell$; the two product squares, arbitrary $X$, and qcqs $g$ are exactly its hypotheses. It proves that $\alpha_{\mathbf F_\ell}(UV,UW)$ is an isomorphism. Now [lem-kun-flat-coefficient-tensor-exchange-comparison] for $\mathbf F_\ell\to k$ identifies this map with scalar restriction of $\alpha_k(\widetilde V,W)$. The scalar-extension first factor agrees with $\widetilde V$ after pullback by Step 1. Conservativity of that restriction shows that $\alpha_k(\widetilde V,W)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, existing prime-field theorem and general coefficient tensor identity

proof.text:
Use the retract $V\xrightarrow{s}\widetilde V\xrightarrow{t}V$ from Step 7. Naturality of the counit-defined comparison of Step 1 gives $B_k(s)\alpha_k(V,W)=\alpha_k(\widetilde V,W)A_k(s)$ and $B_k(t)\alpha_k(\widetilde V,W)=\alpha_k(V,W)A_k(t)$. Consequently
$$A_k(t)\,\alpha_k(\widetilde V,W)^{-1}\,B_k(s)$$
is an inverse of $\alpha_k(V,W)$: composing on either side and using these two identities gives respectively $A_k(ts)=1$ and $B_k(ts)=1$. This proves the finite-field case; no division by $[k:\mathbf F_\ell]$ is used.

The finite filtration of Step 6 and the two-out-of-three argument of Step 1 now prove the comparison for every flat $\Lambda$-sheaf $\mathcal E$ and every $\Lambda$-sheaf $\mathcal F$. Step 4 proves it for arbitrary bounded-below $F$. Steps 2 and 3 then prove that the original comparison induces an isomorphism in every degree $q$. Its endpoints are bounded below: the original K-flat model is zero below $n$, the model for $F$ and $Rg_*F$ is zero below $b$, so both endpoints are in $D^{\ge n+b}$ by Step 1. After forgetting coefficients their cohomology-stalk maps are isomorphisms, so [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] makes the forgotten comparison invertible. The conservative forgetful functor of [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison] reflects this invertibility. All reductions used the specified counit map, so this is the map in the statement.
